subject: Computer Networking
title: VPNs for Network Security
description: Learn VPNs for Network Security in one minute.

hook.text: A remote worker connects to the office from a coffee shop. Without a VPN, their traffic crosses the open internet.

buildup.text: A VPN creates an encrypted tunnel. All traffic between the worker and the office travels through it safely.

discovery.text: IPsec and WireGuard are common VPN protocols. They authenticate both ends and encrypt every packet.

twist.text: VPNs trust the endpoint completely. If a worker's laptop is compromised, the VPN gives the attacker full access.

climax.text: That's why zero-trust architecture is replacing VPNs. Verify every request, not just the tunnel.

punchline.text: A VPN protects the pipe. Zero trust protects every drop.

quiz.question: What security limitation do VPNs have?
options: A compromised endpoint gets full network access through the tunnel
VPNs only work on wired connections

details.summary: VPNs create encrypted tunnels over the internet, making remote connections as secure as being on the local network. Site-to-site VPNs link offices together, while remote-access VPNs let employees work securely from anywhere. VPN protocols like IPsec and WireGuard handle encryption transparently.
details.whyItMatters: VPNs are essential for secure remote work and connecting distributed offices. They extend the trusted network perimeter to wherever employees are working.
takeaways: VPNs encrypt all traffic through a tunnel over the internet
Site-to-site VPNs connect entire office networks securely
WireGuard offers simpler, faster VPN connections than IPsec

faq.question: What is the difference between a site-to-site and remote-access VPN?
faq.answer: Site-to-site VPNs create a permanent encrypted link between two networks, like connecting branch offices. Remote-access VPNs let individual users connect to the corporate network from anywhere.

faq.question: Is a VPN the same as zero trust?
faq.answer: No. VPNs give full network access once connected, trusting everything inside the tunnel. Zero trust verifies every request regardless of network location, granting access only to specific resources. Many organizations are moving from VPN-based access to zero trust architectures for better security.
